```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 8  # sources
    J = 6  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [112, 111, 100, 137, 103, 248, 249, 88]
    demands = [44, 31, 46, 46, 60, 25]
    cost_matrix = [[29.86, 10.52, 4.99, 26.04, 8.17, 28.49], [17.83, 11.77, 8.96, 9.51, 8.8, 27.19], [21.36, 27.27, 20.89, 13.8, 12.05, 3.82], [16.33, 24.48, 9.79, 7.03, 18.28, 25.63], [27.65, 8.36, 28.76, 24.12, 22.39, 19.21], [22.65, 21.99, 8.72, 15.41, 10.28, 19.94], [28.0, 23.2, 16.31, 23.39, 10.83, 27.77], [8.99, 12.71, 8.65, 21.52, 4.52, 20.01]]
    emission_matrix = [[9.37, 3.87, 8.4, 16.75, 18.85, 15.36], [12.87, 15.39, 16.37, 15.08, 18.33, 11.74], [9.73, 8.28, 3.36, 18.8, 5.88, 18.12], [7.93, 1.0, 20.0, 14.5, 6.24, 2.08], [11.01, 8.18, 15.95, 11.47, 3.98, 18.19], [8.11, 15.38, 10.15, 2.1, 16.11, 12.28], [9.45, 14.34, 9.77, 11.6, 10.87, 4.66], [7.78, 5.96, 11.01, 4.0, 14.57, 13.44]]
    fixed_costs = [[255, 114, 164, 289, 270, 264], [83, 86, 218, 235, 207, 253], [259, 54, 125, 236, 179, 271], [101, 71, 102, 212, 225, 270], [196, 173, 62, 215, 155, 204], [213, 62, 213, 112, 290, 215], [182, 66, 180, 194, 192, 61], [130, 125, 118, 76, 196, 68]]
    moq = [[18, 16, 9, 18, 16, 15], [19, 18, 13, 8, 19, 16], [20, 11, 11, 14, 16, 7], [5, 20, 18, 20, 13, 12], [18, 6, 12, 15, 6, 10], [6, 8, 9, 6, 14, 16], [18, 7, 17, 17, 12, 19], [20, 8, 17, 9, 20, 17]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Executive Supply Chain Leadership

Date: [Insert Date]
Subject: Balancing Delivered Cost and Carbon in Our Warehouse-to-Store Shipping Plan

Context
Our next shipping plan must protect margin while advancing our sustainability commitments. Each warehouse‑to‑store route is evaluated on both a dollar cost per unit and a CO2 emission rate per unit. In practice, lower‑cost lanes often have higher emissions (e.g., longer distances, older equipment, or more transloads), while the cleanest lanes can carry a price premium. We need a plan that delivers reliably and meets demand without exceeding inventory, while striking the right balance between cost and carbon.

Operational Rules and Realities
- Route activation costs: Turning on any lane requires an upfront setup cost (contracting, customs, and dock arrangements). A lane is either active or not; if active, we incur this setup cost regardless of shipped volume.
- Minimum order quantities on active lanes: Once a lane is activated, we must ship at least a specified minimum to justify load building and handling; partial truckloads are not accepted on these lanes.
- Supplier limits per store: To manage receiving capacity and vendor complexity, each store may receive deliveries from no more than a set number of warehouses. This cap must be respected in any plan.
- Supply and demand discipline: Shipments cannot exceed available inventory at each warehouse, and each store’s minimum demand must be met on time.

Management Priorities
Leadership has established relative importance weights for cost and emissions. We will evaluate any proposed plan using a combined score that:
- Applies the specified importance weight to the total variable shipping cost across all active routes.
- Applies the specified importance weight to the total emissions across all active routes.
- Adds the setup cost for every lane we activate at its full value (these setup costs are not weighted).
This blended score reflects how we value savings and carbon reductions across the network.

Decision Required
We need to determine:
- Which warehouse‑to‑store routes to activate, and
- How much to ship on each active route,
such that we meet store demand without exceeding warehouse inventory, honor minimum order quantities on any activated route, and keep the number of supplying warehouses per store within the allowed cap. Among all plans that satisfy these rules, we will select the one with the lowest combined cost‑and‑carbon score as defined above.

What Success Looks Like
- Demand is fully covered and service is protected.
- Warehouse inventory limits are respected.
- Activated lanes each carry at least their required minimum volume.
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of warehouses.
- The resulting plan achieves the lowest blended score given our stated priorities, acknowledging the trade‑off that some cleaner lanes may cost more and some cheaper lanes may emit more.

Next Steps
Once the attached data are confirmed, the team will generate a recommended plan and highlight key trade‑offs (e.g., how changes in route activation or supplier limits affect both delivered cost and carbon). We will also prepare a brief set of alternatives illustrating different balances between cost and emissions using the same rules.
